source.quote: On the OAuth apps tab, select Create OAuth app.

oauthAppCreation.where: Calendly Profile menu > Developer > OAuth apps > Create OAuth app (or developer.calendly.com)

source.quote: In Calendly, open the Profile menu and select Developer.

reviewGate.trigger: The docs describe Sandbox and Production app types that the developer picks, and no review. Absence of a documented review is not proof that none exists.

source.quote: Environment type: select Sandbox for development and testing, or Production when your app is ready for real users.

approvalWait.stated: No approval process or wait is documented

testBeforeApproval.how: Create a Sandbox app for development, then a separate Production app for real customer data

source.quote: We recommend that you start with a Sandbox app for development. Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.
scheduled_events:read Retrieve scheduled events and event invitee information.
event_types:read Retrieve event type details and available times.
webhooks:write Create or delete webhook subscriptions.
scheduling_links:write Create a single-use scheduling link from an existing event type without any customization.

blockers.summary: A new OAuth app has no API access until scopes are explicitly requested

source.quote: no API access is granted until scopes are explicitly requested and approved

blockers.summary: Production apps accept only https redirect URIs, and each app takes exactly one redirect URI

source.quote: Redirect URI: the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app. Enter exactly one URI.

blockers.summary: Sandbox and Production are separate apps, so going live means creating a second app

source.quote: Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.

avoidProducts.name: Calendly MCP server
avoidProducts.why: The MCP server uses dynamic client registration instead of a pre-registered OAuth app
avoidProducts.evidence: Appeared in web search results for the Calendly OAuth docs (2026-10-29)

notes: Calendly is the thinnest golden entry: no review or wait is documented, so both are low confidence. A guide that says Unknown for the wait is correct, and a guide that invents a number is wrong.
Webhooks may need a paid Calendly plan according to a search summary, but no official page fetched here states it, so it is not recorded as a blocker.
